dedupe_keys.name: jonathan mcdowell s list of enormous and large satellite constellations

description: Jonathan McDowell's Space Pages keep a running list of planned and deployed satellite mega-constellations, compiled by the astrophysicist best known for his General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects (GCAT) and Jonathan's Space Report. The list of enormous constellations covers systems with more than 1,000 planned satellites, such as Starlink, Kuiper, OneWeb, the Chinese Guowang (Xingwang) and Qianfan systems and others, about 30 in all, and a companion list covers large constellations of 50 to 1,000 satellites. For each constellation it gives the operator and country and, shell by shell, the altitude, inclination, number of planes and satellites per plane as defined in filings with the US Federal Communications Commission or the International Telecommunication Union, together with the number of satellites currently on station and links to launch histories and statistics pages. The page was updated on 24 September 2026. Coverage: worldwide filings and deployments. Format and access: web pages with tables, free; the related GCAT catalogue is downloadable as text files under an open licence. Caveats: compiled by one person; filings often overstate what will be built, and ITU filings of up to about 200,000 satellites are included as filed. Simulation uses: scenarios of future satellite broadband and positioning capacity, congestion and collision risk studies, and exposure of constellations to space weather. Related records: CelesTrak and ESA DISCOS cover objects in orbit, and the ITU Space Network List covers frequency filings.
